title: FDM miniature support evidence and experimental principles
scope: 28–32 mm gaming miniatures and small parts, single-material PLA, primarily 0.2 mm nozzle; proposed experiments are not physical print validation.
conclusion: The best-supported starting architecture is a hybrid: printable small contacts and local island anchors, stable FDM branches, and broader removable interfaces where the first model toolpaths need them. No reviewed source establishes a universal best resin-style support profile for arbitrary 32 mm miniatures. Treat native organic/tree and snug slicer supports as serious controls, and select a Pareto frontier of intact detail, underside quality, removal effort, time and material rather than minimizing contact count alone.

provisional_process.evidence: The user has confirmed an A1 with 0.2 mm nozzle. Root agent found 0.06 mm High Quality and Bambu PLA Matte selected in local BambuStudio.conf; those selections do not confirm the intended physical spool or final process.
hold_constant: Filament brand, color, batch and moisture condition
Actual first layer and later layer heights
Cooling, minimum layer time, speed and acceleration
Model orientation and scale within a comparison
Support removal tools, order and cooling time
provisional_process.geometry_export_note: Our support meshes are ordinary model geometry. Native slicer support Z distance, interface count and support wall loops do not automatically alter them. Encode intended geometry in the export and inspect the actual sliced toolpaths; generic model wall/infill settings may govern the exported trees.

evidence_scale.A: Primary implementation/documentation establishes software behavior, not print success on our hardware.
evidence_scale.B: Peer-reviewed or creator-performed physical work, useful within its tested process and geometry.
evidence_scale.C: First-party workflow or product demonstration, without controlled cross-model measurements.
evidence_scale.H: Our hypothesis or preregistered experimental criterion, not an established optimum.

sources.title: Prusa: Support material
sources.finding: Top contact clearance, interface density and XY separation affect separation and underside support. Nonzero contact clearance causes the initial model layer to use bridging behavior. Independent support layers can follow contact clearance more precisely.
sources.limits: Its suggested contact distances are PrusaSlicer guidance, not a transferable recipe for imported geometric supports or Bambu at 0.06 mm.

sources.title: Prusa: Organic Supports
sources.finding: Lower branch angles and thicker branches improve stability; close branch spacing increases contact and removal difficulty. Dense interfaces are recommended over simply increasing branch density when a dense roof is needed.
sources.limits: Descriptive software guidance; the page's broad claims about scar-free removal are not controlled measurements across miniatures.

sources.title: OrcaSlicer: Support Advanced
sources.finding: Z distances are rounded to layer multiples unless independent support height applies. Interface layers/spacing control the dense roof. Tree bridge suppression uses a maximum span and requires anchoring at both ends. Organic support does not offer independent support layer height in this documentation.
sources.limits: Wiki edited October 14, 2026. Installed versions may differ; record the actual executable version and generated toolpaths. Settings concern slicer-generated support.

sources.title: OrcaSlicer: Wall Generator
sources.finding: Arachne varies line width. Minimum feature size can discard small features; features retained below minimum wall width are widened. Minimum wall length can remove short isolated segments.
sources.limits: A visible mesh tip is not proof of an extruded tip. Lowering thresholds can preserve geometry without establishing reliable extrusion.

sources.title: Prusa: Printing great-looking miniatures with a 0.25mm nozzle
sources.kind: manufacturer's own miniature printing guide and examples
sources.finding: Demonstrates 28/32 mm miniatures with a small nozzle; discusses fragile accessories, limited contact area, slower printing, and cooling benefits of printing more than one figure. Model-specific support settings and sliced-preview checks are emphasized.
sources.limits: Older Prusa MINI and 0.25 mm examples, including materials outside our PLA scope. Do not transfer temperatures, extrusion reductions or angle numbers without calibration.

sources.title: Clonephaze: Resin2FDM Walkthrough
sources.finding: Resin2FDM starts with pre-supported resin geometry, separates it, thickens supports, repairs meshes and exports separately configurable geometry. Tip detection and structural reinforcement are provided.
sources.limits: Useful comparator workflow, not evidence that a specific tip size wins. Presupport quality is an uncontrolled input. Search-index content was available; direct full-page fetch intermittently timed out.

sources.title: Dumas, Hergel and Lefebvre: Bridging the Gap: Automated Steady Scaffoldings for 3D Printing
sources.kind: peer-reviewed SIGGRAPH/ACM TOG paper, author-hosted summary
sources.finding: Considers overhang support and stability throughout printing. Uses bridges supported at both ends and pillars to reduce material while improving the reliability of sparse hierarchical support.
sources.limits: An older process and different test models; it motivates stability and bridge-aware design, not a quantitative 0.2 mm miniature recipe.

sources.title: OrcaSlicer: Tree Support
sources.finding: Documents separate angle/diameter settings by tree style, density/removal tradeoffs and wider brims for taller, thinner trees. Lower preferred angles favor vertical stability.
sources.limits: Native trees have specialized toolpaths. A mesh exported as a model does not inherit these semantics.

sources.title: Wang, Wu, Liu and Yu: Deposition path-dependent lightweight support design and its implication to self-support topology optimization
sources.kind: peer-reviewed Journal of Computational Design and Engineering paper
sources.finding: Chooses support locations using deposition-path curvature and allowable unsupported length rather than surface geometry alone.
sources.limits: Investigates panel structures and contour-offset paths with dissolvable supports; adapting the idea to breakaway PLA miniatures remains a hypothesis.

sources.title: FDM Forge product description
sources.finding: Advertises sparse resin-style trees, separate support geometry and routing fallbacks. Its marketing describes gravity as the only failure mode.
sources.limits: No controlled numerical comparison found. The gravity-only premise is incomplete for extrusion printing: toolpath formation, cooling, print motion, nozzle encounters and removal loads must be considered. Do not use this marketing as validation.

sources.title: Bambu Studio issue 7967: Resin-style supports generated natively
sources.finding: The author reports some successful resin-presupport prints on a P1S, but also thin supports, scarring and processing mistakes requiring reprints.
sources.limits: Anecdote, no controlled sample size, no accepted implementation or recommended preset; useful failure-mode evidence only.

sources.title: Fat Dragon Games: DRAGONLOCK Miniatures Adventurers
sources.finding: The designer explicitly targets FDM printing without slicer supports.
sources.limits: A supportless model is a process/detail control, not a challenging test of our support algorithm. Do not treat popular FDG process profiles as proof of arbitrary resin-model support quality.

sources.title: Clonephaze: Resin2FDM FAQ and Glossary
sources.finding: Suggests 0.3–0.6 mm tips and 1.2–2 mm supports as starting ranges, strengthening columns before enlarging scars, and cross-bracing isolated pillars. Separates failures during extrusion, travel and string pulling; recommends small test parts first.
sources.limits: Not a controlled study and no universal process is specified. The page also suggests changing slicer support interface count, which does not by itself modify ordinary imported support meshes, and broadly dismisses floating-region warnings; we reject those blanket interpretations. Check final toolpaths and alignment individually.

engine_audit.status: Code inspection only; no physical prints performed by this research task.
existing_strengths: Extra anchors for islands that grow quickly from a small first cross-section
Minimum separation to reduce crowded tip crowns and a central contact row under narrow blades
Branches, braces, foot groups and self-support checks
Explicit collision, trapped support and unstable trunk diagnostics
engine_audit.interpretation: The code contains physical-print failure notes and deliberate FDM-specific improvements. The upstream README also states that systematic print validation is lacking. There is insufficient evidence to judge the author's expertise; investigate limitations of the method and profile instead.
engine_audit.profile_mismatch: The current nozzle_02 profile uses 0.08 mm analysis layers and 0.22 mm line width. The app entry point overrides gap, angle and raft but not layer height. A locally selected 0.06 mm slicer process therefore need not match the analysis grid.
engine_audit.contact_math: For cone tips, tree.py computes endpoint = surface_point - surface_normal * tip_penetration - [0,0,z_gap]. At a horizontal downward face, nominal vertical separation = z_gap - tip_penetration. Current app gap 0.03 and profile penetration 0.03 therefore produce a touching nominal endpoint, not a 0.03 mm air gap. Curved/sloped faces, finite tip sections and sliced layers require a fuller intersection analysis.
engine_audit.caution: A passing triangle/slice-geometry checker is a necessary engineering gate, not proof that the final slicer's extrusion sequence, cooling, adhesion or removal will succeed. Root reports the historical 53-part run had error issues on 19 parts; that benchmark establishes performance, not print quality.

principles.principle: Validate the deposited paths, not just the support mesh.
principles.application: For every critical island and contact, inspect the final slicer's first model extrusion, last support extrusion, intervening Z clearance and nearby XY anchors. Record missing crowns and isolated tiny paths.
principles.failure: Mesh contact exists but the slicer omits its crown, widens it into an unintended weld, or starts the model on an unsupported path.

principles.principle: Separate vertical clearance from intentional penetration and match the actual layer grid.
principles.application: Use explicit zero-penetration gap experiments, record first-layer height and actual sliced clearance. Retain the exact current app as a control rather than silently relabeling it.
principles.failure: A nominal gap change produces no distinct sliced condition, or a supposedly detached contact remains merged.

principles.principle: Differentiate a new island, an expanding overhang and a bridge with two anchors.
principles.application: Do not exempt an isolated hand or one-ended sword merely because it is short. Anchor a newly appearing component before its perimeter grows, and preserve sufficient later contacts for that growth.
principles.failure: The first island layer floats, a short cantilever is classified as a bridge, or an island fails while later coverage looks adequate.

principles.principle: Use the contact shape and density that the underside requires.
principles.application: Sparse contacts can suit small, curved or hidden features; a broad cape or shield underside may need a local roof. Compare quality against native interfaces instead of assuming resin-style points always win.
principles.failure: Low contact counts look good in preview but leave sagged first perimeters, missing detail or larger surface defects than the interface control.

principles.principle: The tip must print reliably and still be the preferred break location.
principles.application: Express candidate crown diameters in line-width units, confirm the final paths, and measure both survival and removal damage. A larger crown can help deposition while increasing bonding and scars.
principles.failure: Tip disappears, strings or breaks during printing; or removal damages the miniature before separating the tip.

principles.principle: Supports need a stable route to the bed throughout the print.
principles.application: Check branch self-support, trunk height/width, non-collinear feet, bracing and bed adhesion. Make higher trunks stronger without indiscriminately enlarging model contacts.
principles.failure: Floating brace/branch layer, tall narrow group, bed detachment, lateral wobble or knocked-over support.

principles.principle: Plan removal access as part of routing.
principles.application: Route away from faces, fingers, blade edges and enclosed cavities where possible. Require a cut/peel path; a collision-free tree can still be mechanically trapped.
principles.failure: Removing supports needs bending a delicate part, leaving inaccessible debris or cutting visible model detail.

principles.principle: Orientation is a multi-objective support decision.
principles.application: Compare upright and modest tilts that move scars off the face and improve island growth while checking weapon layer strength, support height and print time. Do not prescribe a universal 45-degree resin tilt.
principles.failure: A lower support-area orientation increases face scarring, weak-axis breakage, unreachable contacts or unstable high trees.

principles.principle: Calibrate overhangs and bridges for the real process.
principles.application: Use measured span and per-layer lateral step limits. Engine angles are measured from vertical; never copy an angle from another slicer without converting its convention.
principles.failure: Thresholds permit ragged unsupported edges or bridge spans that droop under the chosen filament, fan and path direction.

principles.principle: Cooling, extrusion and motion are part of support reliability.
principles.application: Hold minimum-layer-time, speed, acceleration and travel policy fixed in the first sweep. Compare more than one plate position and distinguish heat damage from support failure.
principles.failure: An apparent geometry improvement disappears when plate order, cooling time or motion changes.

principles.principle: Protect full-resolution geometry at contact placement.
principles.application: Use simplified meshes for broad search, then verify contacts and thin islands against original geometry. This is our engineering inference: a proxy error comparable to a gap can change support contact or miss a small detail.
principles.failure: A proxy-only pass places a contact in empty space, clips a blade or loses an original-mesh island.

principles.principle: Rank success by usable miniatures, not a single proxy metric.
principles.application: Treat failed prints and broken features as failures. Among intact prints compare underside defects, visible scars, hands-on cleanup, support material and time. Use repeated prints before claiming a general improvement.
principles.failure: A faster or lower-contact setting is promoted despite worse detail, removal damage or reliability.

test_cases.name: Tip and crown ladder
test_cases.geometry: Small supported horizontal tabs and round-bottom islands with otherwise identical trunks.
digital_checks: Top two crown layers contain nonzero extrusion
test_cases.note: These diameters are exploratory candidates, not known optima. Keep tip base >= tip diameter.

test_cases.name: Gap, penetration and layer phase
test_cases.geometry: Flat tabs and sloped undersides; repeat after shifting the model/support assembly in Z by half a nominal layer in a controlled project.
controls: Exact current app .08 analysis/.03 gap/.03 penetration
digital_checks: Measure last support and first model path heights
Verify exported parts keep a shared frame
physical_metrics: Detachment force or consistent ordinal effort score
test_cases.note: Z phase experiment is digital first; re-slicing may reposition objects, so record actual geometry and paths.

test_cases.name: Growing island and one-ended weapon
test_cases.geometry: Hanging hand/ball of about 2–3 mm radius; 0.6–1.2 mm blade or wrist; two-ended bridge and equal-length one-ended cantilever.
digital_checks: Every new disconnected model component has a printable anchor
Follow growing component for at least 1 mm
test_cases.note: Anchor-off is a diagnostic negative control; it is not a recommended production setting.

test_cases.name: Point roof versus interface
test_cases.geometry: 6–12 mm cape/shield underside plus curved underside from a real miniature.
controls: Native tree/organic supports with top interfaces
digital_checks: Measure unsupported portions of initial underside paths
test_cases.note: Flat coupon success is not enough: repeat on a curved actual part.

test_cases.name: Tall forest stability
test_cases.geometry: Comparable 20, 30 and 40 mm support groups, including feet in a line and a wider triangular group; real raised-arm miniature.
digital_checks: Foot-group minimum width and aspect ratio
No model collision outside designated contacts
test_cases.note: Thicker/braced combination is a screening package; isolate its variables if it wins.

test_cases.name: Removal corridor
test_cases.geometry: Bent arm against torso, between-leg gap, sword beside cloak and an open versus closed cavity.
digital_checks: No support imprisoned by model loop
Contacts avoid fragile edges when alternatives exist
test_cases.note: A 3D mesh collision test alone cannot establish accessibility.

test_cases.name: Orientation sweep
test_cases.geometry: Same chosen head, weapon arm and complete miniature, preserving source scale.

variables.axis: Choose an axis that moves contacts toward hidden surfaces; record it and handedness explicitly.

digital_checks: First islands, support height and accessible routes
test_cases.note: These are test orientations, not a universal mini-support rule. Use the same exact geometry in each comparison.

test_cases.name: Bridge and overhang calibration
test_cases.geometry: Paired-anchored spans 1, 2, 4, 6 and 8 mm; stepped sloped faces at 45, 55, 65 and 75 degrees from vertical; thin edge variants.
digital_checks: Record path direction and real anchor length
Separate bridge, overhang and island classifications
test_cases.note: Use results to choose process-specific limits; do not assume every short gap is bridgeable.

test_cases.name: Plate and cooling repeat
test_cases.geometry: A small challenging part repeated at front/center/back, plus a tall thin weapon on two different print runs.
digital_checks: Record traversal order and layer times
test_cases.note: Multiple copies on one plate are correlated. A later repeat run is needed for stronger reliability evidence.

test_cases.name: Proxy sensitivity
test_cases.geometry: Original high-detail head, thin blade and a small disconnected ornament; compare analysis proxies at increasing error tolerance.
digital_checks: Contact signed distance to original surface
Collision checks on original geometry near every tip
physical_metrics: Only finalists need printing; all must pass original-geometry audit
test_cases.note: If proxy error equals a meaningful fraction of tip gap/diameter, original-mesh verification becomes mandatory.

test_cases.name: Held-out collection challenge
test_cases.geometry: At least a head, weapon arm, complete mini, broad cape/shield and tall thin feature selected from the user's collection; freeze files, scale and orientation in a manifest.
test_cases.note: Tune on coupons and one part; hold back at least two different real parts. A digital pass cannot mark the physical test as passed.

innovation_hypotheses.name: Layer-aware contact placement
innovation_hypotheses.hypothesis: Choosing contact Z and crown dimensions using the actual slicer layer grid will reduce missing crowns and accidental welds more consistently than a continuous mesh gap.
innovation_hypotheses.near_term: Sweep penetration=0 and gaps 0/.06/.12, process-matched layer height and .26/.36/.46 crowns; record actual toolpaths.
innovation_hypotheses.implementation_after_evidence: Snap or optimize contact crowns against first-layer height plus layer grid, with original-mesh clearance checks.
innovation_hypotheses.falsifier: No improvement in intact detail/removal at equal material, or benefits disappear after a half-layer phase change.
innovation_hypotheses.status: Hypothesis; initial ablations use existing params.

innovation_hypotheses.name: Feature-specific micro-interfaces
innovation_hypotheses.hypothesis: A small tear-away roof under broad or highly curved underside paths will improve finish while retaining sparse points under isolated hidden details.
innovation_hypotheses.near_term: Compare dense point settings against native tree-interface and snug controls to establish whether our missing roof is the limiting factor.
innovation_hypotheses.implementation_after_evidence: Generate one or two printable roof layers only where first-path span/curvature exceeds a calibrated limit; give the roof an accessible peel edge.
innovation_hypotheses.falsifier: Roof fusion/removal scars outweigh reduced sag, or point supports perform equally at lower cost.
innovation_hypotheses.status: Hypothesis; native interfaces provide a feasible comparator, new roof geometry is not implemented here.

innovation_hypotheses.name: Load-aware trunks with small break tips
innovation_hypotheses.hypothesis: Thickening and widening the support load path according to height and supported island growth can improve survival without increasing all contact scars.
innovation_hypotheses.near_term: Compare current settings to stronger branches/trunks and tighter braces while preserving tip geometry; use anchor-on versus anchor-off only as a diagnostic.
innovation_hypotheses.implementation_after_evidence: Use growing-component area, height and support group footprint to assign local branch/brace strength rather than one global dense preset.
innovation_hypotheses.falsifier: Extra structure does not improve failures, or removal force is transmitted into fragile model features.
innovation_hypotheses.status: Hypothesis; substantial components already exist in ArborFDM, so contribution would be calibration/adaptation, not invention of bracing.

innovation_hypotheses.name: Path-aware bridge and contact placement
innovation_hypotheses.hypothesis: Contacts aligned to where the first real underside paths turn or lack two-sided anchors will outperform uniform spacing for equal support volume.
innovation_hypotheses.near_term: Compare blade versus broad roof and two-ended bridge coupons; measure unsupported path lengths from final G-code.
innovation_hypotheses.implementation_after_evidence: Add a slicer-informed contact pass or conservative contour-path approximation, using measured bridge limits.
innovation_hypotheses.falsifier: Benefit depends on one infill angle and fails with another ordinary slicer path ordering.
innovation_hypotheses.status: Hypothesis; research transfer from different geometry and materials, not a proven miniature result.

innovation_hypotheses.name: Removal-aware routing and orientation
innovation_hypotheses.hypothesis: Scoring visible scar area, weak-feature leverage and removal corridors will yield more usable miniatures than optimizing support volume alone.
innovation_hypotheses.near_term: Orientation sweep of head/arm/complete mini; compare hidden-side contacts and removal time with fixed tip settings.
innovation_hypotheses.implementation_after_evidence: Add face-sensitive contact penalties, an optional protected-region brush and cuttable branch corridors; preserve a controlled fallback when no accessible route exists.
innovation_hypotheses.falsifier: Additional hidden contacts cause trapped supports or weaker printed weapons with no reduction in visible damage.
innovation_hypotheses.status: Hypothesis; orientation and some trapped-support checks already exist upstream.

innovation_hypotheses.name: Coarse search with original-detail contact refinement
innovation_hypotheses.hypothesis: A cheap whole-model proxy plus high-resolution local checks near islands/tips can retain browser speed while preventing proxy-induced placement mistakes.
innovation_hypotheses.near_term: Run proxy-sensitivity tests and score original-mesh contact error on thin parts.
innovation_hypotheses.implementation_after_evidence: Refine candidate contacts, tiny disconnected features and narrow gaps on original triangles; regenerate only implicated support regions.
innovation_hypotheses.falsifier: Original-mesh failures remain or refinement erases the performance benefit without improving physical results.
innovation_hypotheses.status: Our engineering hypothesis; not established by the wall-generator documentation, which only motivates attention to tiny features.

baseline_controls.name: Exact deployed app
baseline_controls.purpose: Measures improvement over what the user already has.
baseline_controls.configuration: Freeze commit, nozzle_02_normal, actual UI values and original orientation; retain 0.08 mm analysis rather than silently matching it to 0.06.

baseline_controls.name: Process-matched app
baseline_controls.purpose: Separates layer-grid correction from new geometry ideas.
baseline_controls.configuration: Same as B0 except analysis layer height matches the selected 0.06 mm process; explicitly record raft thickness/release gap instead of changing them accidentally.

baseline_controls.name: Native Bambu tree
baseline_controls.purpose: Strong practical baseline in the user's existing slicer.
baseline_controls.configuration: Original model only; native supports enabled, fixed style/angle/interface settings saved with the project. Include stock process support values and one calibrated Z-gap/interface variant. Do not add native supports around the app's exported trees.

baseline_controls.name: Native snug or normal interface
baseline_controls.configuration: Original model only, same filament, orientation, layer height and motion; save exact clearance, interface count/spacing and XY separation.

baseline_controls.name: Native organic tree
baseline_controls.purpose: Avoid a straw-man comparison against untuned tree settings.
baseline_controls.configuration: Use an installed slicer/version that supports Organic. Keep top interfaces enabled for the first control; save settings. Do not infer that an identically named field behaves identically across slicers.

baseline_controls.name: Supportless FDM mini or robust process coupon
baseline_controls.purpose: Distinguishes extrusion/cooling/detail problems from support problems.
baseline_controls.configuration: Print an owned or freely licensed design intended for supportless FDM with the same process. This is a control, not a challenge benchmark.

baseline_controls.name: Converted resin presupports, optional
baseline_controls.purpose: Tests the claimed resin-to-FDM workflow when a matching presupported source is owned and available.
baseline_controls.configuration: Use the same mini, scale and orientation where possible, with a documented Resin2FDM conversion. If different presupport orientation is required, report it as a workflow comparison, not an isolated algorithm experiment.

experiment_protocol.status: Research and proposed experiments only. User asked to review research before further algorithm implementation or sweep production; no implementation or physical validation is implied by this document.
experiment_protocol.candidate_collection_cases: Root inventory identified a bare arm, spanner hand and complete Spore on a 32 mm base as a useful first set. Preserve their file hashes, native dimensions and chosen orientations in the eventual manifest.
experiment_protocol.phase_1: Digital gates: source/geometry integrity, self-support checks, original-mesh contacts and actual slicer path inspection. Label each variant as passed, failed, or unverified at each gate.
experiment_protocol.phase_2: A small coupon screen to choose viable gap and tip ranges. Preserve zero/touching as a control; do not start by combining every proposed improvement.
experiment_protocol.phase_3: Compare the best two app variants and native slicer baseline on held-out collection parts, with at least three copies per condition spread over two runs if practical. Rotate or randomize plate locations with a recorded seed.
experiment_protocol.phase_4: Confirm the winning tradeoff on a complete difficult miniature and the user's multi-part plate. Record actual print duration and cleaning effort.
measurement_rules: Photograph every part before cleanup and after the same initial cleanup procedure, with the same light, scale and views.
Log failed prints and damaged features, not just surviving examples.
Keep unsupported sag, scar/pit damage and ordinary layer lines as separate categories.
Use blind variant labels where practical; retain the mapping in the manifest.
Do not normalize a scale-model collection by overall bounding-box height without checking whether a weapon or base dominates that measurement.
Claim a candidate only when it improves a chosen quality/removal metric without a worse failure rate; a few successful copies are screening evidence, not a precise reliability estimate.
Generated 3MF, successful slicing and a rendered screenshot mean ready to test, never physically validated.
